🇮🇷🇺🇸 Is the Iran war paused or just reloading? Why chokepoints like Hormuz never stay quiet for long

Michael Yon, a former Green Beret turned war correspondent, says the quiet around Iran looks like the lull in a firefight, when the first magazines are empty and everyone is reloading and shifting position. He doesn’t count any of it as a ceasefire:

“There is no pause in this war.”

His argument is geography.

Hormuz, Panama and Suez sit on trade routes the world can’t do without, so he calls them standing wars, places that get fought over for centuries whoever holds office.

Panama took about 400 years and four failed attempts before the canal opened in 1914.

So Michael puts no weight on memorandums or off-ramps, and he expects the fighting to spread to other straits, with Japan high on his list.
